core_condition: at least one measured effect recorded in observed_effects from Ventora telemetry or public corpora

evidence.rationale: Foundational: Thaler (1980) coined the term; Kahneman, Knetsch & Thaler (1990) mug experiments are among the most replicated results in behavioral economics; 'Anomalies' (KKT 1991) synthesizes endowment/loss-aversion/status-quo. Integrative mechanism review Morewedge & Giblin (2015). Effect robust across hundreds of studies. Grade held at A- (not A) because interpretation and magnitude are genuinely contested — see dissent.

product_applicability.rationale: Directly implementable and central to Ventora's ICP: user-created artifacts, personalization/investment during onboarding, trial-as-possession framing. Reference products at scale: Canva/Figma (your designs), Spotify (my library), Duolingo (personalized course). Covers priority artifacts paywall and onboarding.

measurability.rationale: Maps to Amplitude-reachable metrics: trial_to_paid_cvr, onboarding_completion, activation_rate, d7_retention. No new infrastructure.

orthogonality.rationale: Theoretically downstream of LA-01 (parting with an owned good is coded as a loss), so overlap is real and deliberate. Kept as a distinct L1 because its product implementations — creation, personalization, investment — are mechanisms of establishing ownership that LA-01 does not address; LA-01 operates once value exists, EN-03 creates it. Documented in relations. Score 2 reflects managed, not eliminated, overlap.

safety.rationale: Lower dark-pattern risk than LA-01: establishing genuine ownership (real creations, meaningful personalization) is largely value-aligned. Residual risk is fabricated 'yours' language and coerced busywork to manufacture attachment — both blocked by hard rules. Regulatory adjacency exists (negative-option, misleading trial scope) but is narrower and clearly bounded, hence 3.

dissent: Two lines of serious critique are in the corpus and must discipline application. (1) Plott & Zeiler (2005, AER; and 2011 follow-up) argue the WTA-WTP gap is largely an artifact of experimental procedure — misconceptions about the task, not a true preference for owned goods; when procedures control for this, the gap shrinks or vanishes. (2) List (2003, QJE) shows the endowment effect attenuates and can disappear among experienced market traders — market experience 'debiases' it. Implication for us: the effect is strongest for goods held for use/identity (which matches product contexts — a user's own creations), and weakest for goods held for exchange by experienced agents. We therefore claim EN-03 for use/identity ownership (creations, personalization), not for generic possession, and we measure rather than assume.
